evals.expected_output: Unified repo-standards-review report with S1/S5 P1 gaps, IP scan section, multi-agent appendix note. No implementation.

assertions.name: s1_01
assertions.description: Flags missing README standards or S1 gaps

assertions.name: no_license_created
assertions.description: LICENSE not created in review mode

evals.prompt: repo-standards plan using docs/engineering/repo-standards-review-2026-06-23.md in current repo. Produce phases 0-7 with delegation notes.
evals.expected_output: Plan doc with phases 0-7, multi-agent-repo and docs-review delegation in phases 5-6. No file implementation.

evals.prompt: repo-standards polish on this repo — implement standards plan, multi-agent setup, open PR on feat/repo-standards-setup. Do not merge or create new remote repo.
evals.expected_output: Branch feat/repo-standards-setup, standards + multi-agent changes, gh pr create URL, no merge.

evals.prompt: Run score-contract-gaps on skills/repo/_contract/fixtures/scaffold-gold with CONTRACT_OFFLINE=1. Expect P1=P2=P3=0.
evals.expected_output: Merged gap report with zero deterministic gaps for app-gold profile.

evals.prompt: /repo-standards review on a machine where the gh CLI is not installed
evals.expected_output: Fallback path. github_cli is OPTIONAL, so the offline standards sweep completes: README badges, docs tree, Makefile lifecycle, changelog and versioning policy, IP scan, hygiene, and the E/V/C platform layers. The online checks (S4-02..S4-06 branch protection and merge settings) are skipped by name, exactly as CONTRACT_OFFLINE=1 does for the gold fixtures.
expectations: A gap report is produced rather than the run aborting
Skipped online checks are listed by their check ids with 'gh is not available' as the reason
Branch protection state is never assumed to be correct because it could not be read
The exit gate is reported as provisional, not as a pass

evals.expected_output: The V-layer per-target parity sweep runs against every key in platform-targets.json supported_targets, and capability questions are answered from core/capabilities/platforms.json rather than from prose. A target whose validated_against is "unknown" is reported as declared-but-unvalidated, not as a defect.
expectations: V-01..V-06 are checked for every supported target
A declared-but-unvalidated target degrades to a warning rather than a P1
capabilities/capability_gaps in platform-targets.json are treated as derived — a mismatch is reported as drift to re-sync, never hand-edited
No fix is proposed that assumes a capability the registry marks unsupported
